question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=-\frac{1}{3}$ cannot be solutions since division by $0$ is undefined. 

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{6x-3} & =\frac{2}{3x+1} \\ 9\cdot (3x+1) & =(6x-3)\cdot 2 \\ 27x+9 & =12x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}27x+9 & =12x-6 \\ 27x+9-12x & =12x-6-12x \\ 15x+9 & =-6 \\ 15x+9-9 & =-6-9 \\ 15x & =-15 \\ \frac{15x}{15} & =\frac{-15}{15} \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $x=-1$ is different from $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we can accept it as a solution.
Thus, the solution is $x=-1.$
